title: Man's Impact on the Environment
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Man's Impact on the Environment Worksheets (3Rs, PSLE Practice)
standard_code: Primary 6: Interactions within the environment (Man's impact on the environment)
standard_text: Recognise how man's activities, such as clearing forests, pollution and burning fuels, affect the environment and living things, and how man can conserve the environment through the 3Rs (reduce, reuse, recycle), conservation of habitats and saving resources (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on man's impact on the environment: deforestation, pollution, global warming, the 3Rs and conservation. PSLE practice with answers.
key_big: People can harm or protect the environment.
key_sub: Reduce, reuse and recycle to cut waste.
body_html:
How to think about it

People can harm the environment, but people can also protect it.

  • Harm: clearing forests destroys habitats; air, water and land pollution harm living things.
  • Burning fuels adds carbon dioxide to the air. This leads to global warming.
  • The 3Rs: reduce (use less), reuse (use again), recycle (make into something new).
  • Conservation: nature reserves, planting trees, saving water and electricity.
Example

Using an empty jam jar to store buttons is which of the 3Rs?

The jar is used again, not made into something new

Answer: reuse

Example

Why does clearing a forest harm animals?

Think about food and shelter

Answer: They lose their habitat, food and shelter.

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up reuse and recycle. Recycling makes the material into something new.
  • Thinking clearing a forest only affects the trees. The animals lose their habitat too.
  • Saying global warming is caused by the hole in the ozone layer. It is mainly caused by more carbon dioxide.
  • Thinking rubbish that is burnt disappears. The ash still goes to Semakau Landfill.

faq.a: Reduce (use less), reuse (use again) and recycle (make old materials into new things).

faq.q: How does cutting down forests affect the environment?
faq.a: Animals lose their habitats, soil is washed away, and fewer trees take in carbon dioxide.
Mainly more carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases in the air from burning fuels and clearing forests.

items.q: Which of these is caused by man?
c: a river flooding after heavy rain
leaves rotting on the forest floor
a tree falling in a storm
clearing a forest to build houses
items.e: People change the environment in many ways.

items.q: Hafiz observes: “Forests are cleared for new houses.” What impact can this have?
c: animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
algae blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish
warmer water with less oxygen for fish
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: A park connector with trees links two parks. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: Protecting habitats helps living things; destroying or polluting them causes harm.

items.q: What does 'reduce' mean in the 3Rs?
c: making something new from old material
items.e: Reduce is the best of the 3Rs.

items.q: Rubbish is thrown into a monsoon drain. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: This destroys or disturbs a habitat, so living things are harmed.

items.q: A forest is cleared to build a factory. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: This destroys or disturbs a habitat, so living things are harmed.

items.q: Coral reefs are damaged by boats dropping anchors on them. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: This destroys or disturbs a habitat, so living things are harmed.

items.q: Pupils pick up litter at East Coast Park. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: Protecting habitats helps living things; destroying or polluting them causes harm.

items.q: Kumar observes: “Cars and factories burn fossil fuels.” What impact can this have?
c: warmer water with less oxygen for fish
animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
air pollution and more carbon dioxide
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Bright lights are left on all night near a beach where turtles nest. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: This destroys or disturbs a habitat, so living things are harmed.

items.q: Where does much of Singapore's rubbish ash go after the rubbish is burnt?
items.e: Semakau Landfill is filling up, so we need to reduce waste.

items.q: What is the difference between reusing and recycling?
c: Reusing uses an object again; recycling makes the material into something new.
items.e: A jam jar used again is reused; a melted jar is recycled.

items.q: People release unwanted pet terrapins into a reservoir. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: This destroys or disturbs a habitat, so living things are harmed.

items.q: A town builds more cycling paths so people drive less. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: Protecting habitats helps living things; destroying or polluting them causes harm.

items.q: Fishermen use nets that also catch turtles. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: This destroys or disturbs a habitat, so living things are harmed.

items.q: What causes the haze that sometimes reaches Singapore?
c: smoke from forests and peatland being burnt in the region
items.e: It is a form of air pollution.

items.q: Which of these helps to conserve water?
c: washing the car with a running hose
turning off the tap while brushing your teeth
items.e: Singapore also uses NEWater and desalinated water.

items.q: How does cutting down forests affect animals?
c: They lose their food and shelter.
items.e: Clearing forests destroys habitats.

items.q: Green roofs with plants are built on top of buildings. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: Protecting habitats helps living things; destroying or polluting them causes harm.

items.q: Why does cutting down many trees increase the amount of carbon dioxide in the air?
c: Fewer trees take in carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
Trees give out carbon dioxide only.
Carbon dioxide comes from the soil.
items.e: Burning the trees also releases carbon dioxide.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by burning forests that cause haze?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by fireworks set off near a bird sanctuary?
items.e: Loud sounds disturb people and animals.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by oil spilled from a ship?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the water.

items.q: Which of these causes water pollution?

exhaust fumes from cars and buses
old furniture dumped at the back of a block of flats
loud music played near a nature reserve
items.e: Chemicals from a factory poured into a river leads to water pollution.

items.e: Honking horns in heavy traffic leads to noise pollution.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by switching off the lights when you leave a room?
items.e: Reduce means using less in the first place.

items.q: Zhi Hao's family throws away 4 kg of rubbish a day. How much rubbish is this in one week?
items.e: 4 kg × 7 days = 28 kg.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by using old newspapers to wrap fragile things?
items.e: Reuse means using something again without changing what it is made of.

items.q: Hafiz's family throws away 35 kg of rubbish in 10 days. If they recycle 25% of it instead, how much less rubbish goes to be burnt?
Which of the 3Rs is shown by giving old clothes to a younger cousin?
items.e: Reuse means using something again without changing what it is made of.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by collecting glass bottles so they can be melted and made into new glass?
items.e: Recycle means the material is made into something new.

items.e: 40% of 15 kg = 6 kg.

items.e: Recycle means the material is made into something new.

items.e: Reuse means using something again without changing what it is made of.

items.q: Ravi's family throws away 2.5 kg of rubbish a day. How much rubbish is this in one week?
items.e: 2.5 kg × 7 days = 17.5 kg.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by turning a plastic bottle into a plant pot?
items.e: Reuse means using something again without changing what it is made of.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by taking a shorter shower?
items.e: Reduce means using less in the first place.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by passing old textbooks to pupils in the next class?
items.e: Reuse means using something again without changing what it is made of.

items.q: Kumar's family throws away 35 kg of rubbish in 10 days. If they recycle 20% of it instead, how much less rubbish goes to be burnt?
items.e: 20% of 35 kg = 7 kg.

items.q: A nature reserve is set up to protect a forest. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: Protecting habitats helps living things; destroying or polluting them causes harm.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by buying only the food your family will eat?
items.e: Reduce means using less in the first place.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by turning food waste into compost for plants?
items.e: Recycle means the material is made into something new.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by bringing your own bag to the supermarket?
items.e: Reduce means using less in the first place.

items.q: Why are electric buses better for the air in a city than diesel buses?
c: They do not give out exhaust fumes on the road.
items.e: Fewer exhaust fumes means cleaner air.

items.q: Which of these causes noise pollution?
items.e: Construction work all night leads to noise pollution.

items.q: Which of these is a renewable source of energy that does not pollute the air?
c: solar energy from panels on HDB rooftops
items.e: Solar panels change light energy into electrical energy.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by detergent washed into a drain?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the water.

items.q: How can burning less fuel help the environment?
c: Less carbon dioxide and fewer harmful gases go into the air.
items.e: Taking the MRT instead of a car burns less fuel per person.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by sending old newspapers to be made into new paper?
items.e: Recycle means the material is made into something new.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by smoke from a ship's engine at sea?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: Which of these causes noise pollution?
c: plastic bags left in a park
loud music played near a nature reserve
items.e: Loud music played near a nature reserve leads to noise pollution.

items.q: Why should plastic bags not be thrown into the sea?
c: Turtles may swallow them and die.
items.e: Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down.

items.q: What is global warming?
c: the hole in the ozone layer
the slow rise in the average temperature of the Earth
items.e: It is mainly caused by more greenhouse gases in the air.

items.q: Why are nature reserves such as Sungei Buloh important?
c: They are only for building houses.
They are places to dump rubbish.
They protect habitats so plants and animals can survive.
items.e: Conservation keeps many populations alive.

items.q: Oil spilled from a ship coats the feathers of seabirds. What happens to the birds?
c: They cannot fly or keep warm, and may die.
items.e: Oil spills are water pollution.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by putting used paper cartons into the recycling bin?
items.e: Recycle means the material is made into something new.

items.q: Which action helps to save electricity?
c: setting the air-conditioner to 25 °C and closing the windows
keeping lights on in empty rooms
leaving the TV on standby all night
items.e: Making electricity usually means burning fuel.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by sending plastic bottles to be made into new plastic?
items.e: Recycle means the material is made into something new.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by loud music played near a nature reserve?
items.e: Loud sounds disturb people and animals.

items.q: Which gas is mainly linked to global warming?
items.e: Burning fuels releases carbon dioxide.

items.q: Why does Singapore encourage people to bring their own bags when shopping?
c: to reduce the number of plastic bags thrown away
items.e: This is an example of 'reduce'.

items.q: A canal is lined with concrete and its plants removed. What is the most likely effect on the environment?
c: It has no effect on living things.
items.e: This destroys or disturbs a habitat, so living things are harmed.

items.q: Why is a rise in sea levels a problem for Singapore?
c: Low-lying coastal land could be flooded.
The sea would become fresh water.
items.e: Melting ice and warmer water raise sea levels.

items.q: Why does planting trees in a city help to cool it?
c: Trees give shade and lose water vapour from their leaves.
items.e: Green spaces are cooler than bare concrete.

items.q: Which of these causes land pollution?
c: old furniture dumped at the back of a block of flats
paint washed into a monsoon drain
items.e: Old furniture dumped at the back of a block of flats leads to land pollution.

items.q: A forest next to a stream was cleared. After heavy rain, the stream became muddy. Why?
c: Without tree roots, the soil was washed into the stream.
The trees made the stream clean.
items.e: Roots hold soil in place; this is soil erosion.

items.q: Which of these causes air pollution?
c: old batteries thrown into the soil
items.e: Burning rubbish in the open leads to air pollution.

items.q: Which change would best reduce the amount of rubbish sent to Semakau Landfill?
c: Families throw recyclables into the rubbish bin.
Families reduce, reuse and recycle more of their waste.
items.e: Less waste means less ash.

items.q: A school collected 40 kg of paper for recycling each month. How does this help the environment?
c: More rubbish goes to the landfill.
Fewer trees need to be cut down to make new paper.
items.e: Recycling saves raw materials.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by exhaust fumes from cars and buses?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by rubbish dumped in a forest?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the land.

items.q: A canal had many fish. After a factory poured waste into it, many fish died. Which is the most likely reason?
c: The waste polluted the water and reduced the oxygen in it.
items.e: Pollution harms the organisms in the habitat.

items.q: Which of these causes land pollution?
c: paint washed into a monsoon drain
fireworks set off near a bird sanctuary
exhaust fumes from cars and buses
items.e: Litter left on a beach leads to land pollution.

items.q: Which of the 3Rs is shown by using the back of old worksheets for rough work?
items.e: Reuse means using something again without changing what it is made of.

items.q: Ahmad wants to know whether a recycling programme reduces rubbish. What is the best way to monitor this?
c: ask one neighbour what they think
check once on a single day
weigh the rubbish sent to the landfill each week before and after
items.e: Monitoring uses measurements over time, before and after.

items.q: Why should used batteries be put into the e-waste bins instead of the rubbish chute?
c: They can be eaten by birds.
They contain chemicals that can pollute the land and water.
items.e: Batteries can be recycled to recover metals.

items.q: What happens to the population of animals when their habitat is destroyed?
c: It decreases because they lose food and shelter.
items.e: Animals depend on their habitat.

items.q: Which of these causes air pollution?
c: plastic bags left in a park
paint washed into a monsoon drain
items.e: Burning forests that cause haze leads to air pollution.

items.q: Which of these is an example of conserving a habitat?
c: keeping Bukit Timah Nature Reserve protected
clearing a forest for a car park
filling in a pond to build a road
items.e: Protected areas keep habitats safe.

items.q: Wei Jie's family throws away 2 kg of rubbish a day. How much rubbish is this in one week?
items.e: 2 kg × 7 days = 14 kg.

items.q: Mangrove trees along a coast were cut down. Which is the most likely result?
c: The coast is worn away more by waves, and animals lose their habitat.
items.e: Mangroves protect coasts and are habitats.

items.q: Arjun wants to know whether a new bus line reduces air pollution. What is the best way to monitor this?
c: ask one neighbour what they think
measure air quality and traffic for several months before and after
check once on a single day
items.e: Monitoring uses measurements over time, before and after.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by litter left on a beach?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the land.
